messages:
tara (support): Customer reported 300-800ms extra latency for APAC users and a burst of 401s this morning. They say they pin to ap-southeast-1 but traces show hits to us-east-1. billing spike too. Any quick ideas?
matt (support): can you paste a sample request-id and the api_key? don’t post secret in public thread, a masked key or first/last 4 is fine. also which customer account?
tara (support): request-id=rid_0a9f3b2c, app_key=kl_****_z9 (customer acct: acct-847). Happened between 08:12-08:28 UTC. Attached pcap and a few trace IDs in DM.
jess (eng-sre): saw the same in routing logs. interestingly the route policy for acct-847 evaluated as if the first entry was missing, so fallback went to primary us-east pool. i'm seeing repeated parse warnings: "Skipping unknown token at position 0" from route-parser v2.4.3.
jess (eng-sre): repro snippet I used locally:```bash
curl -s -X POST https://route-eval.redwood.test/eval \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer test-token" \
  -d '{"policy": "\uFEFF[ {\"region\": \"ap-southeast-1\", \"weight\": 100}, {\"region\": \"us-east-1\", \"weight\": 0} ]" }' | jq
```
jess (eng-sre): note the payload contains a BOM (\uFEFF) at the start of the array — our YAML->JSON conversion script introduced a leading zero-width BOM in some policies during the last console rollout. that BOM makes the JSON string not start with '[' so the parser drops the first element. result: priority list shifts left.
eli (infra): confirmed a deploy at 2026-03-16T07:59:12Z that updated config-converter. deploy-bot: ``deploy v2.18.0 -> config-converter`` (see log). this lines up with customer impact window.
deploy-bot: deployment v2.18.0 to config-converter finished at 2026-03-16T07:59:12Z (sha: d4f7a2).
eli (infra): mitigation options: 1) roll back config-converter to v2.17.x (fast) 2) set ROUTE_PARSER_STRICT=true to reject BOM'd policies so console will fail writes (safer for small window) 3) patch parser to trim BOM (but that’s a code change). i'd push 1+2 asap.
matt (support): jess, can you confirm whether tokens bound to region cause the 401s? customer says same api_key works in APAC normally.
jess (eng-sre): yes — auth service expects region-scoped routing info for some keys. when requests land in us-east the auth lookup returns no mapping -> 401. this is why some requests succeed (those that hit ap-southeast) and others don't.
sam (billing): because traffic was served out of us-east, egress and cross-region costs spiked. I’m pulling the invoice delta now. if we confirm the rollout caused misrouting we should offer a billing credit for the excess egress.
jess (eng-sre): temporary customer-side workaround: add an explicit override policy via control-plane API that reorders the array and is uploaded without going through the broken converter. example:```bash
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.test/api/v1/overrides \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer OA-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"account":"acct-847","policy":[{"region":"ap-southeast-1","weight":100},{"region":"us-east-1","weight":0}],"note":"temp override to bypass converter"}'
```
jess (eng-sre): after override I saw evaluation route to ap-southeast-1 immediately in the eval logs. also run `redis-cli HGET router:policy:acct-847 current` to verify the stored policy (should show no leading BOM).
matt (support): i'll coordinate with customer to apply the override now and monitor. sam, please flag billing team for credit review. eli, can infra roll back config-converter?
eli (infra): rolling back now to v2.17.4, will notify when done. also enabling ROUTE_PARSER_STRICT in console cluster to prevent new bad writes.
sam (billing): got it — opening a credit ticket referencing acct-847 and the deploy id. will follow up with a proposed credit amount after the delta is computed.
tara (support): applied override, customer reports tail latency back to normal and no new 401s for ~10m. they still want postmortem + confirmation on credits. thanks all. :raised_hands:
matt (support): we'll draft a short incident note and follow up with customer. tagging @oncall to include in postmortem.
jess (eng-sre): followups: 1) add BOM trimming in parser with a unit test 2) add a console validation step to reject non-printable leading chars 3) run a scan for policies containing \uFEFF across DB and auto-fix. I'll put PRs up.
tara (support): perfect. closing loop with customer now, will paste their acceptance in this thread.
